title: Book One · Chapter 48: A Page for Each Person
story:
Miss Wu wants the class to make a book. Each child will choose a familiar place for a page. Each child will have one page. A place can be a room, a corner, or a shop. A small place is fine. It can be important to just one person.

Ronan wants to bring the street map. “Half of it is mine,” Leo says. Both boys want it on their page.

“You each worked on a part. Show your own part,” Miss Wu says. “Don't copy one page twice and call it two jobs.”

Ronan decides to write about the green gate and yard. Leo chooses the station road. His father uses that road. They can look at the map for help. Each boy still needs to write his own page.

Mei chooses the thread shop. She likes the rows of small coloured reels. “The shop is on our map already,” Ronan tells her.

“Your map doesn't own the shop,” she says.

“I didn't mean that.”

“What did you mean?”

He isn't sure. The step and side door were on his map. He wanted to show them to Mei. But Mei saw that same doorway, too. She can draw it better than Ronan.

“I could show you the step mark,” he says.

“I saw the step on my visit.”

She isn't being rude. She went into the shop with her aunt. She saw the step herself. Ronan looks down. He did not think about her visit before.

The children start their pictures. Ronan tries to draw their green gate. It looks like a box with a line down it. Mrs Lan's front window becomes a smaller box. The black cat looks like a dropped sock.

Mei sees it and smiles.

“Can you make the cat better?” he asks.

“I can show you a shape on another piece. You draw your own.”

She draws two triangles and a curve. Ronan copies the idea, not her exact lines. His cat is still strange, but it is standing on feet now.

“Can you help with the big map another day?” he asks.

“Maybe. I'd want my name on the drawing part.”

“Of course.”

“And I won't draw every door. That's boring.”

Ronan nods. Mei can help with some pictures. She does not want to draw all the doors. Her answer is clear. Ronan remembers his promises to Jun. His answers were not so clear then.

At home, he writes four sentences about the yard. Mum checks one spelling. “Read your sentences first,” Dad says. “Then you can draw more.”

Ronan reads about the tap, the plant, the window, and the cat. He did not write about Mrs Lan yet. He writes a fifth sentence about Mrs Lan. She lives at the front. Mrs Lan and Ronan's family share the yard.

“Does she want to be in the picture?” Mum asks.

Ronan goes to ask. “You can draw my chair,” Mrs Lan says. “But don't put my face by that cat. It looks like a bag!”

He laughs and improves the cat once more. The chair goes under the front window. Mrs Lan checks the picture. “That chair can sit very still,” she says.

The next day, Miss Wu puts his page beside Leo's. Mei's bright thread shop is three pages farther on. Ronan knows some places in the book. He never went to the other places.

He turns the pages carefully. Other people have small steps, front windows, and favourite corners, too. He knows some of these places already. Other children noticed different things. Those details are new to him. He stops at one new picture. Tomorrow he can ask its maker about it.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：copy＝抄写；own＝自己的；curve＝曲线；shape＝形状。

辅助理解：triangle＝三角形；reel＝线轴；Mrs Lan and Ronan's family share the yard.＝Mrs Lan和Ronan一家人共用院子。

理解问题：

1. 老师为什么要求每个人都写自己的内容？
2. Ronan 和 Mei 在地图图画上怎样谈妥署名？
